wave: Wave 5 — Chẩn đoán hướng người dùng (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_OMP_UPGRADE.md:602-618; work item tại :1976-2045). one_line: Add a key-name redactor (camelCase-normalised, so `apiKey` / `api_key` / `API-KEY` all match), a crash ring persisted through the already-present-but-unused `getCrashLogPath()`, and a `/bug-report` command that assembles a sendable archive in which session transcript content is opt-in and never on by default.
user_visible_effect: A new `/bug-report` command builds a diagnostics archive and shows its path. The archive always carries metadata, per-model cost attribution, failed-assistant-turn diagnostics, and recent crash records; the conversation transcript and its working directory are included ONLY when the user explicitly asks, and delivery is an explicit choice (write archive locally vs. hand it off) rather than an automatic upload. A crash that kills a session is recorded and surfaced on the next start instead of vanishing, and no key whose name looks credential-bearing survives into the archive.

test_contract:
The observable contract is: a value whose KEY NAME is credential-bearing never survives `redactJsonValue`, whatever the key's spelling, and a value whose key name is ordinary is never touched. Both directions are asserted. The specific failure each case defends: (1) `apiKey` is the case that catches a resolve-only port — drop the camelCase→snake_case `.replace()` and this one alone goes red, silently, because `SENSITIVE_KEY` needs a `-`/`_`/start boundary before `api...` and `apiKey` supplies none. (2) proves the delimiter variants still match, so a later edit that tightens the anchors does not quietly narrow the rule. (3) proves `redactUrl` recurses into a nested scheme instead of falling through `new URL` and returning the input unchanged, which is what happens without the first line of the function. (4) is asserted as BOTH halves in one test — the secret param becomes `<redacted>` AND the harmless param is byte-identical — because over-redaction and under-redaction are opposite failure modes and a one-sided assertion can only ever catch one of them. (5) proves the sweep is recursive rather than top-level, so a config-shaped object with a nested `authorization` is covered. (6) asserts the bundle CONTAINS a known non-secret diagnostic field, not merely that secrets are absent: absence-only assertions pass trivially against an empty bundle and would have certified a redaction function that deletes everything. (7) asserts the required absence of `session.jsonl` from `bugReportFiles` without opt-in — the contract that a transcript, which is user data, is never bundled by default.

The consumer who breaks if this regresses is the person who runs `/bug-report` and attaches the archive to a public issue. A false negative here hands their API key to everyone who reads the issue; a false positive merely hides a harmless field. The bias must therefore lean hard toward over-redaction — and the tests must be written so a regression is loud, which is exactly why case (6) exists.

effort: Smaller than the plan's M once the existing surfaces are accounted for, because roughly half the plan's file list already exists in another shape. The genuinely new code is: `redact.ts` (~60 lines, a near-verbatim port), `crash-log.ts` (~120 lines, a port minus the extension-stack matcher), `bug-report.ts` collectors and file list (~200 lines), one command entry (~50 lines), and the redaction matrix (~150 lines). The plan's M rating assumed the bundle-and-archive layer was greenfield; it is not — `packages/coding-agent/src/debug/report-bundle.ts` (380 LOC) already assembles system info, sanitised env, config, logs, session and artifacts into an archive, and `sanitizeEnv` in `debug/system-info.ts` already redacts. The new work is the redaction contract, the opt-in gate, the crash ring, and outward delivery — not archive assembly. The LLM summary is the one piece that could balloon if the single-pass model call turns out to need retry plumbing; keep it behind the same opt-in as the transcript and treat it as skippable.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is shipping the camelCase→snake_case normalisation as optional or "cleanup" rather than as load-bearing — the code still passes review and still passes every test except case (1), and the failure is silent because `apiKey` merely fails to match a regex that no one re-reads. The second is treating `metadata.session.included` as the opt-in gate rather than the two structural gates in `bugReportFiles` and the collector; it reads like a flag, so a future edit that sets it without gating the payload leaks the transcript while every test still passes. The third is assuming the plan's `pi-ref/...` paths resolve from the ultraworkers root — they do not, pi-ref is a separate checkout at `/Users/tranquangdang21/Projects/pi-ref/`, and an engineer who cannot find the file will reconstruct the contract from prose and will probably drop the normalisation without ever realising it was there. The fourth is defaulting the transcript ON because the existing `/debug` report bundle already ships `session.jsonl` unconditionally — that is a pre-existing local-tool behaviour, not a precedent for a bundle whose whole purpose is to leave the machine.
open_questions: Should the crash ring reuse the existing `getCrashLogPath()` (`~/.omp/agent/omp-crash.log`), as the plan instructs, even though it will hold a JSON array under a `.log` extension? pi writes JSON to `crashes.json`. The plan explicitly says to use the existing zero-consumer helper, so the default here follows the plan — but if a human prefers a matching `.json` name, that is a one-line addition to `packages/utils/src/dirs.ts` plus a note that the helper is no longer zero-consumer. Decide before writing the file, not after.

pi's `findExtensionStackMatches` (crash-log.ts:47-113, ~65 lines) maps a stack trace back to the extension that caused the crash. omp's extension model is not pi's: the pi-ref source depends on `Extension.sourceInfo.{origin,source,baseDir,scope}`, and omp's extension records are shaped differently. Should this land in W17, or be deferred? The spec here defers it — it is a diagnostic nicety, not part of the redaction contract, and porting it blind is how a wrong shape gets committed.

Delivery: pi offers upload vs. local zip. omp has no configured issue-tracker upload target that this work item establishes. Should W17 ship the explicit local-archive path only, with upload left as a later item, or does a target already exist that this should call? The spec assumes local-archive-only, which satisfies the plan's "explicit choice" requirement without inventing an endpoint.

Should `packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/errors.ts` (`SECRET_KEY` at line 45, `sanitizeData` at line 100) be refactored to delegate to the new `diagnostics/redact.ts`? It is the same contract implemented twice, which AGENTS.md calls a bug — but it is module-private, its substring matching is deliberately looser, and it feeds live MCP error output. Recommendation: do NOT do this in W17 (W17 is additive-only and this would change a live path's output); file it as a follow-up.

plan_corrections.claim: pi's crash-log.ts is the model to port (169 LOC).
plan_corrections.correction: The port source is real (169 LOC, read in full), but ~65 of those lines are `findExtensionStackMatches` plus its two path helpers (`normalizeStackPath`, `stackContainsPath`), which depend on pi's `Extension.sourceInfo.{origin,source,baseDir,scope}` shape. omp's extension records are shaped differently, so that function cannot be ported blind. The genuinely portable core is the other ~100 lines: `CrashRecord`, the 5-record cap, the 7-day `MAX_AGE`, `readCrashLog`, `recordCrash`, `takeUnnotifiedCrash`, `clearCrashLog`. This spec defers the extension matcher — see open_questions.

plan_corrections.claim: The bundle should be zipped, and the delivery choice is upload vs. local zip. (plan lines 1988-1990, 2010-2011)
plan_corrections.verdict: CORRECT, but the plan implies a missing capability that exists
plan_corrections.correction: Zip is available centrally — `writeArchive(destPath, "zip", entries)` in `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/ar`. Do NOT add a dependency: `adm-zip` and `tar` appear in node_modules only as transitive dependencies (`onnxruntime-node` depends on adm-zip; `fastembed` depends on tar) and NO workspace package.json declares either. Also do not port pi's hand-rolled `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/zip.ts`, which builds a classic ZIP with `deflateRawSync` by hand — that is a duplicate of a central helper AGENTS.md explicitly forbids.
plan_corrections.evidence: `ls node_modules | grep -i zip` -> adm-zip, modern-tar, tar. `git grep -n '"adm-zip"|"tar"|modern-tar' -- 'packages/*/package.json' package.json` -> no matches. bun.lock:1031 shows adm-zip under onnxruntime-node; bun.lock:1165 shows tar under fastembed. `packages/utils/src/ar/write.ts:39-42` handles `case "zip": return encodeZip(members);`.

plan_corrections.claim: pi's LLM-written conversation summary is part of the bundle. (plan lines 1988-1989, 2012-2013)
plan_corrections.verdict: TRUE, but the port must NOT be verbatim
plan_corrections.correction: pi holds the summary prompt as two inline template-literal constants, `BUG_SUMMARY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` and `BUG_SUMMARY_INSTRUCTIONS` (bug-report.ts:316-333). AGENTS.md forbids building prompts in code — prompts must live in static `.md` files with Handlebars for dynamic content, imported `with { type: "text" }`. So this prompt must be extracted to `packages/coding-agent/src/prompts/diagnostics/bug-summary.md` during the port. Its four-section structure (What the user was doing / What went wrong / Steps to reproduce / Relevant details) and its closing constraint ('Do not include file contents, secrets, or credentials from the transcript; refer to files by path only') should be preserved verbatim in the .md file.
plan_corrections.evidence: pi-ref bug-report.ts:316-333 defines both constants as backtick template literals. AGENTS.md 'Prompts' rule. The `with { type: "text" }` convention is confirmed at `packages/coding-agent/src/advisor/advise-tool.ts:13` and `auto-thinking/classifier.ts:18`.

plan_corrections.claim: The plan does not state where the crash writer attaches, and implies a raw process handler. (plan lines 2004-2006, silent on wiring)
plan_corrections.correction: omp already funnels SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/uncaughtException through `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/postmortem`. Adding a raw `process.on("uncaughtException")` would race the existing teardown and is a regression risk. The correct attachment points are `postmortem.register(id, callback)` (line 661) for the cleanup/exit path and `interceptUnhandledRejections(interceptor)` (line 453) for rejections that would otherwise kill the session. Note also that `packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-teardown.ts` is referenced in comments at `modes/interactive-mode.ts:1600` and `extensibility/extensions/managed-timers.ts:7` but does NOT exist at HEAD — do not look for it.
plan_corrections.evidence: `grep -n '^export' packages/utils/src/postmortem.ts` -> `fatal` at :530, `interceptUnhandledRejections` at :453, `register` at :661. `git grep -rn 'uncaughtException' -- packages/coding-agent/src packages/utils/src` -> no process.on("uncaughtException") registration anywhere. `sed -n` on packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-teardown.ts -> 'No such file or directory'.

plan_corrections.claim: W17 introduces the redaction contract as if nothing comparable exists in omp. (plan lines 1978-1980)
plan_corrections.verdict: INCOMPLETE — a prior art exists and must be named
plan_corrections.correction: omp already ships a key-name redactor: `SECRET_KEY` declared at `packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/errors.ts:45` (regex literal on line 46) and a recursive `sanitizeData` at :100 that replaces values under matching keys with `[redacted]` (the replacement is at :117), with depth/entry caps and cycle detection. It is module-private — `grep -n '^export' packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/errors.ts` shows neither is exported. It is deliberately LOOSER than the plan's rule (substring match, no camelCase normalisation, and its comment says compound names like `clientSecret` and `signingSecret` must classify as secrets). So W17 is a port-and-strengthen, not a first implementation, and the new module should be the one that carries the stricter, boundary-anchored rule. Per AGENTS.md the two implementations are a duplication to retire eventually, but the mcp one feeds live error output, so refactoring it is follow-up work, not W17.
plan_corrections.evidence: `grep -n '^const SECRET_KEY\|^function sanitizeData' packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/errors.ts` -> 45 and 100 respectively; the comment explaining the substring choice is at :43-44. `grep -n 'SECRET_KEY' ` -> the use site is :117 (`result[key] = SECRET_KEY.test(key) ? "[redacted]" : sanitizeData(...)`). `grep -n '^export'` on that file -> 8 exports, none of them sanitizeData or SECRET_KEY. `git grep -rn SENSITIVE_KEY -- packages/` -> zero hits, confirming the plan's exact rule does not already exist.
